thread:
tay: deploy-bot fired on canary embedding service p95 jump after v4.2.1 rollout. auto-revert suggested?

deploy-bot: ALERT v4.2.1-embed-canary: p95=1250ms (3m). Auto-revert threshold=1200ms. Suggested action: auto-revert recommended.

rachel: Auto-revert would flip routing and impact in-flight requests. Let's not auto-revert yet, want to decide scoped vs full rollback.

ethan: Agree. Early indicators point to a change in the quantization flag in the new build causing slower kernel startup on older GPUs. Can we do a targeted rollback of the embedding worker variant only?

infra-oncall: We can route embedding requests for dedicated and hosted to the previous variant: `releasectl route --service=embeddings --from=v4.2.1 --to=v4.2.0 --scope=dedicated,hosted-eu --mode=gradual --duration=5m`

rachel: Do it. Also pin dedicated pools to v4.2.0 to avoid immediate re-scheduling to v4.2.1 until we fix the quant flag. Use reason: "targeted rollback for embedding p95 spike".

infra-oncall: Running pin: `releasectl pin --pool=dedicated-global --version=4.2.0 --reason="embed p95 spike"` -> OK
deploy-bot: NOTE: auto-revert suspended for this thread; manual policy in effect. Will continue to monitor thresholds.

tay: Heads up to Support: this is scoped to embeddings; model outputs unaffected for most customers, but some latency-sensitive embedding calls may have seen delays. @support-bot please prepare a short customer advisory for dedicated customers.

support-bot: Drafting message: "We temporarily scoped routing for embedding requests back to v4.2.0 in response to observed latency on v4.2.1 canary. No data loss; this is a performance mitigation. Expect normal service once fix is deployed. Contact support if you see persistent issues." Will post on approval.

ethan: Tech note: the quant flag default changed to `q4_0` which increases kernel init time on T4-class hardware. Fix: gate the flag behind runtime detection or use `q4_0_fast` patch. Planning a quick build pinned to `q4_0_fast`.

rachel: Good. Estimate 35 min to build + verify in staging. In meantime keep routing pinned and monitor p95. If p95 > 1500ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows, escalate to full rollback of v4.2.1 across all services. Documented rollback command: `releasectl rollback --version=4.2.0 --reason="escalation-embed-p95"`

infra-oncall: Routing command succeeded. Canary embedding traffic now back on 4.2.0 for dedicated and hosted-eu. Monitoring active.

tay: Post a short internal release note entry with timeline and commands executed. I'll own customer comms approval.

support-bot: Customer advisory queued to #customer-notify for review.

ethan: Build completed, running quick perf smoke in staging. If perf stable, we'll push patched v4.2.1+patch and then unpin.

rachel: After unpinning, we should ramp using a traffic-canary of 10% over 15m and watch p95 and error-rate. Also add a KV-cache warmup step in rollout checklist to prevent similar spikes.

deploy-bot: Observability: will add temporary watch rule for embeddings p95 and annotation to the release timeline.

tay: Thanks team. Summary (single source): suspended auto-revert, performed targeted routing rollback for embeddings to v4.2.0, pinned dedicated pools, drafted customer advisory, patch build in progress. If escalation criteria met, infra to run full rollback command above and notify customers. Will follow up with postmortem owners after stabilization. :white_check_mark:
